Subject: Pricing snapshot request — EU transit/residency adders

Hi Aditya / Lauren,

We're mapping out our expected usage for H2 and want an official rate snapshot for Redwood hosted API before we kick off procurement. Two specific asks:

1) If we route all inference to your EU region (data residency requirement), what is the add-on (percentage or per-unit) applied to the standard US-hosted rates?
2) Are there separate "transit zone" premiums (e.g., cross-border egress or transit between zones) that we should budget for?

For context, BrightLayer is planning ~200M tokens / month in steady state, with an initial 6-week pilot at ~10M tokens focusing entirely on EU-only residency.

Can you send a short table with: baseline US hosted rate, EU residency adder (absolute and percent), any zone transit premium, and what a scalable committed-discount schedule looks like (3 tiers)? If possible, include indicative effective per-1k-token pricing for the pilot and for steady state at three commitment levels.

Procurement timeline: aiming to complete vendor eval by Aug 6.

Thanks — Sophie

Subject: Re: Pricing snapshot request — EU transit/residency adders

Hi Sophie — thanks for the clear ask. Putting together a short snapshot (attached) and a few clarifying points so we tailor the numbers to BrightLayer's needs: 

- Residency adder: we typically apply a residency premium when customers require EU-only hosting for both control plane and inference. That premium can be expressed as a percentage of the baseline (commonly 10–20% depending on capacity shape) or as a flat per-token uplift if you prefer absolute math.
- Transit / cross-zone: in most setups where the app + inference are both in a single EU region, there's no additional transit surcharge. Transit premiums typically appear when routing requests between regions or for cross-continental failover.
- Commitment bands: standard sample tiers are 0–50M, 50–250M, >250M tokens / month with increasing discounts applied to the baseline. We can model a pilot discount on top of an enterprise committed rate.

I've attached "Redwood_Prices_Jun2026.xlsx" with: baseline US hosted rates, two residency adder models (percent and flat), and three sample commitment scenarios. A few open items for us to finalize the workbook:

1) Do you need SLA-backed latency SLOs in the EU region? (If yes, that can increase the residency adder slightly.)
2) Is BrightLayer expecting encryption-at-rest with HSM-backed KMS (on-prem KMS)? That can also affect pricing for private tenancy options.

If you confirm those, we'll send a cleaned illustrative quote by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Aditya Rao

Hi Sophie — looping Steph on procurement/commitment questions. Quick summary of what we attached and recommended approach: 

What you'll find in the workbook (high level):
- Baseline US hosted rate: presented as $/1k tokens (column A)
- EU residency adder: two options: 12% percent uplift or a flat $0.0012 / 1k-token uplift (both shown) — pick whichever aligns with your internal unit economics.
- Transit premium: 0 for single-region in-EU routing; 3–6% if cross-region failover configured.
- Commitment example: 6% discount at 50–250M, 12% at 250–500M, 18% >500M (these stack with residency adder).

Suggested next steps for BrightLayer:
1) Confirm whether you need SLA-backed latency in EU (yes/no).
2) Confirm whether control plane must be EU-only (adds complexity).
3) If procurement needs a brief term sheet, we can produce a two-page commercial summary (incl. pilot pricing and terms) for your legal/procurement.
